extra_citations.why: Prop 3.1: a real binary form of degree d with d distinct real roots has real rank d. Re((x+iy)^nu) is such a form, so this is the symmetric counterpart of the r->0 limit of Lemma cost (a clean feature needs nu neurons). Journal version not verified this session, so the bib stays arXiv.

A real binary form of degree n (distinct roots) has real rank n iff it has n distinct real roots. This is the iff version of the symmetric rank fact. The arXiv comment says 'To appear in Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata'; volume and year were not fetched, so check them.

The equality case of Lemma cost (nu pairwise-orthogonal unimodular chain vectors with first entry 1) is a dephased complex Hadamard matrix. The catalogue shows these are unique up to equivalence at orders 2, 3 and 5 (Haagerup) and form a one-parameter family F4^(1)(a) at order 4. That family meets the interval patterns but not the non-interval pattern T={1,3}, which pins down how much of JF the equality case really uses.
